t: Reunited in 1861 after Bartolomé Mitre’s victory at Pavón, under the federal Constitution of 1853 as amended in 1860.
Mass European immigration and exports of beef and grain made it one of the world’s richest countries by 1914.
From 1930 coups, Peronism and economic crises alternated, until democracy returned in 1983 after the Falklands War.
dyk: In the national census of 1914 about 30 per cent of Argentina’s population had been born abroad, twice the share in the United States at the time.
ev: Bartolomé Mitre defeats the Confederation at Pavón, reuniting Buenos Aires and the provinces
Argentina joins Brazil and Uruguay in the war against Paraguay
Julio Argentino Roca leads the Conquest of the Desert
The Sáenz Peña Law introduces secret and compulsory male suffrage
General José Félix Uriburu overthrows Hipólito Yrigoyen in the first military coup
Argentina loses the Falklands War to Britain
Economic collapse ends in riots and a sovereign default

f.predecessor: Argentine Confederation; State of Buenos Aires
